prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” agency for everyone — the right choice depends on your goals, budget, industry and whether you need SEO, paid media, social, creative, product/UX, analytics, enterprise integration, etc.

If you tell me what you need (services, budget, company size, timeline, industry), I can shortlist the best matches. Meanwhile, here are practical things to consider and a few well-regarded agencies with strong San Francisco presence to start your research:

How to pick the right agency
- Define outcomes: revenue lift, leads, brand awareness, retention, app installs, etc.  
- Match specialty to need: SEO/organic, paid media, social/community, content, product/UX, full-funnel growth, or enterprise systems.  
- Check case studies and KPIs (CAC, LTV, ROAS).  
- Ask for references from similar-size clients/industry.  
- Look at team composition (owners vs contractors), reporting cadence, tooling, and contract terms.  
- Budget/commitment: short-term campaigns vs long-term growth partnerships.

Agencies with strong San Francisco presence (by specialty)
- AKQA — experience design, product & digital innovation (good for UX-driven products and campaigns).  
- R/GA — integrated creative + tech (strong for large brands and campaign + product work).  
- Publicis Sapient — digital transformation and enterprise-level marketing/tech integration.  
- Edelman Digital — PR-led digital, influence, and integrated communications.  
- Column Five — content strategy, data visualization and branded content.

Where to verify and compare
- Clutch.co, G2, UpCity for ratings and client reviews.  
- Ask for recent case studies that match your sector and KPIs.  
- Shortlist 3 agencies, run a paid pilot or 30–90 day test to evaluate fit and performance.

If you tell me:
- what specific services you need,  
- your monthly/annual marketing budget, and  
- whether you’re a startup, SMB or enterprise,  

I’ll recommend a tailored shortlist of 3–5 San Francisco agencies and suggest questions to ask each one. Which services and budget bracket are you working with?
